speaker: Unknown
en: And the cost of things is rising faster than wages are increasing.
zh: 而且物价上涨的速度超过了工资增长的速度。

speaker: Unknown
en: So things feel less affordable.
zh: 所以东西感觉更难负担了。

speaker: Unknown
en: to most Americans.
zh: 对大多数美国人来说。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then there's this wealth inequality concern, which I would say is both kind of a perception issue.
zh: 然后还有这种贫富不均的担忧，我认为这既是一种认知问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's definitely policy issues that has allowed it to happen, and we can talk about those.
zh: 肯定有允许这种情况发生的政策问题，我们可以讨论那些。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I think America is in this kind of crisis of classism, this crisis of
zh: 但我认为美国正处于这种阶级主义危机中，这种……危机。

speaker: Unknown
en: us versus them.
zh: 我们对抗他们。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it manifests in a lot of different ways.
zh: 它以许多不同的方式表现出来。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, you know, you had Ray Dalio on.
zh: 所以，你知道，你请到了 Ray Dalio。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if you think about Ray Dalio's kind of like cycle of empires, you know, this is this idea that there's been six empires in the last 500 years, and the United States is on the decline and China's on the rise.
zh: 如果你思考 Ray Dalio 那种帝国循环，你知道，这是一种观点，即在过去 500 年里存在过六个帝国，而美国正在衰落，中国正在崛起。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it can be measured across a number of different dimensions, one of which is this crisis of internal struggle.
zh: 这可以从许多不同的维度来衡量，其中之一就是这种内部斗争的危机。

speaker: Unknown
en: which manifests often with external struggle, the Iran war.
zh: 这通常表现为外部斗争，比如伊朗战争。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, why can't we stop having external wars?
zh: 比如，为什么我们不能停止发动对外战争？

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, you know, a nation that's happy with itself generally doesn't go to war.
zh: 好吧，你知道，一个对自身感到满意的国家通常不会去打仗。

speaker: Unknown
en: A nation that's not happy generally does go to war.
zh: 一个对自身不满的国家通常确实会去打仗。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so a lot of this stuff gets tied up, I think, in this economic distress that the United States is feeling.
zh: 所以我认为很多这类事情都与美国正在经历的经济困境纠缠在一起。

speaker: Unknown
en: My contention...
zh: 我的论点是……

speaker: Unknown
en: which may not be very popular, is that the more government has tried to create services for people and help bring them up the ladder, the more expensive those things get.
zh: 这观点可能不太受欢迎，那就是政府越是试图为人们创造服务并帮助他们向上攀登，这些东西就变得越昂贵。

speaker: Unknown
en: Are you socialism?
zh: 你是社会主义吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Policy in the United States, and this is one of the great lies, and I think there's a series of great lies,
zh: 美国的政策，这是巨大的谎言之一，我认为有一系列的巨大谎言，

speaker: Unknown
en: in U.S. policy over the last half century.
zh: 存在于过去半个世纪的美国政策中。

speaker: Unknown
en: But one of the great lies is that the government will save you.
zh: 但其中巨大的一个谎言是政府会拯救你。

speaker: Unknown
en: The government will help you by giving you these essential services that you want more of.
zh: 政府将通过给予你更多你想要的这些基本服务来帮助你。

speaker: Unknown
en: education, healthcare, housing.
zh: 教育、医疗保健、住房。

speaker: Unknown
en: And as the government has entered into those markets, because remember, there are people making those things, offering those services, and there's someone paying for it.
zh: 随着政府进入了这些市场，因为要记住，有人制造这些东西，提供这些服务，还有人为此买单。

speaker: Unknown
en: So as the government enables more money to flow into those markets, the cost of those things has just gone up.
zh: 所以随着政府让更多的资金流入这些市场，这些东西的成本就只是上涨了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you can see how this plays out, for example, in education.
zh: 你可以看到这在教育领域是如何发生的，例如。

speaker: Unknown
en: So higher education.
zh: 也就是高等教育。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you want to go to college in the United States, and I'll just give you a statistic, 30 years ago, administrative staff were like 10% of colleges.
zh: 如果你想在美国上大学，我就给你一个统计数据，30 年前，行政人员约占学院人数的 10%。

speaker: Unknown
en: Today, they're like 60%.
zh: 今天，这个比例大约是 60%。

speaker: Unknown
en: In just 30 years.
zh: 仅仅在 30 年的时间里。

speaker: Unknown
en: Give me a rational reason why we should have 6x the administrative staffing at colleges and universities.
zh: 给我一个理性的理由，说明为什么我们的学院和大学应该拥有 6 倍的行政人员。

speaker: Unknown
en: There isn't a good reason why.
zh: 并没有一个充分的理由。

speaker: Unknown
en: The real reason is that because the federal student loan program doesn't discriminate against the university on how well they do with their graduating students or the degree or the individual that's taking out the loan, the federal student loan program has just allowed more money to flow in to universities.
zh: 真正的原因是，因为联邦学生贷款计划并没有根据大学对其毕业学生的表现、学位或贷款个人的情况来区分对待大学，联邦学生贷款计划只是允许更多的资金流入大学。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now, if you're a university administrator, there's no constraint on how much you can charge for tuition.
zh: 现在，如果你是一名大学管理者，你对学费能收取多少没有任何限制。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, hey, we'll raise tuition 5% this year.
zh: 所以，嘿，我们今年把学费提高 5%。

speaker: Unknown
en: We'll raise it 8%.
zh: 我们提高 8%。

speaker: Unknown
en: We'll raise it 10%.
zh: 我们提高 10%。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we'll hire more people.
zh: 我们会雇用更多的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if people hire more people, they get a higher salary.
zh: 如果人们雇用了更多人，他们自己就能获得更高的薪水。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you think about the individual, I don't get to make more salary until I'm a manager.
zh: 如果你想想个人层面，我直到成为经理才能拿到更高的薪水。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now I want to be a director.
zh: 现在我想成为主管。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now I want to be a senior director.
zh: 现在我想成为高级主管。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the organization grows.
zh: 然后组织就长大了。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's very natural for any organization, whether it's a nonprofit, a university, or a private company.
zh: 对于任何组织来说这都是非常自然的，无论是非营利组织、大学还是私营公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: You want to grow and people want to make more money year after year.
zh: 你想要增长，人们想要年复一年地赚更多的钱。

speaker: Unknown
en: So they, because they can collect more money, can charge more for tuition.
zh: 所以他们，因为他们能收取更多的钱，就能够收取更高的学费。

speaker: Unknown
en: There isn't a natural market force that says your tuition is too high now because the government has provided unlimited funding to higher education through the federal student loan program.
zh: 并不存在一种自然的市场力量说你的学费太高了，因为政府已经通过联邦学生贷款计划为高等教育提供了无限的资助。

speaker: Unknown
en: So as a result, education has gotten so vastly expensive that everyone now looks at it and says, we got to do something about this.
zh: 所以结果就是，教育已经变得如此昂贵，以至于现在每个人看着它都说，我们必须对此做点什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: And both parties seem to say, well, here's what the government's going to do to do more.
zh: 而且两党似乎都在说，好吧，这就是政府将要做更多事情的方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's like putting fuel on the fire.
zh: 这就像是在火上浇油。

speaker: Unknown
en: So the challenge right now is people are feeling left behind.
zh: 所以现在的挑战是人们感觉被抛在了后面。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's massive wealth inequality.
zh: 存在巨大的贫富不平等。

speaker: Unknown
en: Things are extremely unaffordable.
zh: 各项东西都极难负担。

speaker: Unknown
en: Right.
zh: 对。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the solution that's being embraced is for the government to do more, which de facto leads to socialism.
zh: 而且正在被采纳的解决方案是让政府做得更多，这实际上会导致社会主义。

speaker: Unknown
en: What is wrong with socialism?
zh: 社会主义有什么问题？

speaker: Unknown
en: I would argue that the key measure of a country's success is how many people are transitioning from labor to capital each year.
zh: 我认为一个国家成功的关键衡量标准是每年有多少人正在从劳动转向资本。

speaker: Unknown
en: What does that mean?
zh: 那是什么意思？

speaker: Unknown
en: That means every year I'm working paycheck to paycheck.
zh: 那意味着每年我都在靠薪水度日。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm collecting checks.
zh: 我在领支票。

speaker: Unknown
en: I graduated college.
zh: 我大学毕业了。

speaker: Unknown
en: I had $19,000 in debt.
zh: 我有 19,000 美元的债务。

speaker: Unknown
en: I went and worked.
zh: 我去工作了。

speaker: Unknown
en: I got paid.
zh: 我领了薪水。

speaker: Unknown
en: I saved up.
zh: 我存了钱。

speaker: Unknown
en: I paid down my debt.
zh: 我还清了我的债务。

speaker: Unknown
en: I was able to get out of it.
zh: 我能够摆脱它。

speaker: Unknown
en: Then I worked at Google.
zh: 然后我在 Google 工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: We had an IPO.
zh: 我们进行了 IPO。

speaker: Unknown
en: Suddenly, I had assets.
zh: 突然间，我有了资产。

speaker: Unknown
en: I had stuff.
zh: 我有了东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: I had money in the bank account.
zh: 我银行账户里有钱。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it was like an incredible moment for me.
zh: 这对我来说是一个难以置信的时刻。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I said, I could live off that money.
zh: 我说，我可以靠那笔钱生活。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't need to live off a paycheck every month.
zh: 我不需要每个月靠薪水生活。

speaker: Unknown
en: I now have savings.
zh: 我现在有积蓄。

speaker: Unknown
en: I have assets.
zh: 我有资产。

speaker: Unknown
en: That is capital.
zh: 那就是资本。

speaker: Unknown
en: And everyone talks about capital versus labor.
zh: 每个人都在谈论资本与劳动的对立。

speaker: Unknown
en: But the real advantage of America is enabling people to go from labor to capital.
zh: 但美国的真正优势在于让人们能够从劳动转向资本。

speaker: Unknown
en: Every individual that works, saves, invests, does whatever they need to do to accumulate enough capital ends up in the capital bucket.
zh: 每一个工作、储蓄、投资、做任何他们需要做的事情来积累足够资本的个人，最终都会进入资本的那个桶里。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then you're no longer stuck needing to go paycheck to paycheck to pay your bills.
zh: 然后你就不再被困住，需要靠薪水度日来支付账单。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's the dream.
zh: 那就是梦想。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's the real American dream.
zh: 那是真正的美国梦。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's not just about owning a house.
zh: 这不仅仅是拥有一套房子。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you own a house and you want to have a bunch of debt and you got insurance payments to make and you still got to work every month to make those payments, you're not necessarily living the American dream yet.
zh: 如果你拥有一套房子，而你想要背负一堆债务，你必须支付保险费，而且你仍然每个月必须工作来支付这些费用，那么你未必就已经生活在美国梦中了。

speaker: Unknown
en: The American dream is being freed of that burden.
zh: 美国梦是从那个负担中解脱出来。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because you can live off the interest of your assets.
zh: 因为你可以靠你资产的利息生活。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's right.
zh: 没错。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so you're earning income.
zh: 所以你在赚取收入。

speaker: Unknown
en: Let's say you have $100,000 saved and you can make 10% a year on that.
zh: 假设你存了 100,000 美元，你每年可以从中赚取 10%。

speaker: Unknown
en: Suddenly, if you get to $1 million saved, you can make $100,000 a year and you can live on that.
zh: 突然间，如果你存到了 100 万美元，你每年可以赚 100,000 美元，你可以靠这个生活。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's economic security.
zh: 那是经济安全。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's financial security.
zh: 那是财务安全。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's what we should give to every American is the ability to own assets that give them freedom to choose what they want to do in their life rather than be stuck in work.
zh: 我们应该给每一个美国人的是拥有资产的能力，这给他们自由去选择他们在生活中想做的事情，而不是被困在工作中。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the problem with socialism is it takes away that transition moment.
zh: 社会主义的问题在于它夺走了那个转变时刻。

speaker: Unknown
en: It eliminates it because it says everyone has to be labor all the time for the rest of their lives.
zh: 它消除了那个时刻，因为它说每个人在余生都必须一直做劳工。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then no one has freedom.
zh: 然后就没有人拥有自由。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's what America was founded on was this ability to find through freedom of choice, through agency, the ability to transition from labor to capital.
zh: 这就是美国的建立基础，这种通过自由选择、通过主观能动性找到从劳动转向资本的能力。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think our goal as a country should be get 2% of Americans across that line every year.
zh: 我认为我们作为一个国家的目标应该是每年让 2% 的美国人跨过那条线。

speaker: Unknown
en: Then I think we'll be successful going forward.
zh: 那么我认为我们在未来会取得成功。

speaker: Unknown
en: But if everything's all about like give people more stuff and have the government do it, we're just going to keep raising the debt, making things more expensive, inflating the costs away.
zh: 但如果所有事情都只是关于给人们更多的东西并让政府来做这件事，我们只会继续增加债务，让东西变得更贵，把成本通胀掉。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's inevitable that socialism will happen in America.
zh: 美国发生社会主义是不可避免的。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's absolutely inevitable.
zh: 这是绝对不可避免的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Do you think the U.S. as an empire is in decline?
zh: 你认为美国作为一个帝国正在衰落吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: In terms of the power of the dollar, in terms of prosperity of Americans, the average American, majority of Americans, the answer is yes.
zh: 就美元的力量而言，就美国人的繁荣而言，对普通人、大多数美国人来说，答案是肯定的。

speaker: Unknown
en: But the potential hasn't been deleted, meaning decline is not inevitable.
zh: 但这种潜力并没有被删除，这意味着衰退并非不可避免。

speaker: Unknown
en: To be very clear, we are not yet at a point where it's a runaway train.
zh: 很明确地说，我们还没有到达那种失控列车的地步。

speaker: Unknown
en: In the history of democracies, there's never been a place like America where an individual like myself, moving here from South Africa, going to public college, graduating with debt, and then being able to work my way out of the debt and find myself in the position I'm in today with no nepotism, with no handouts, with...
zh: 在民主的历史上，从来没有像美国这样的地方，一个像我这样的人，从南非搬到这里，上公立大学，带着债务毕业，然后能够通过努力工作摆脱债务，并发现自己处于今天的这个位置，没有裙带关系，没有施舍，拥有……

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, you could argue about privilege and all these other sorts of things that I was vested over my life, but...
zh: 我的意思是，你可能会争论关于特权以及我一生中被赋予的所有这些其他事情，但是……

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, it's an amazing place that that sort of story can be told a million times over, that there's not just one or two people that this has happened to, but there's millions of people.
zh: 比如，这是一个神奇的地方，这种故事可以讲述一百万遍，不仅有一两个人经历过这种事，而是有数百万人。

speaker: Unknown
en: The problem is it's all the other hundreds of millions that didn't get to live that opportunity.
zh: 问题在于所有其他数以亿计的人没有获得那个机会。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if we can fix that, America is not in decline.
zh: 如果我们能解决这个问题，美国就没有在衰退。

speaker: Unknown
en: America is a prosperous nation and has centuries ahead of it.
zh: 美国是一个繁荣的国家，并且还有几个世纪的前程。

speaker: Unknown
en: But when you look at this, you're talking about runaway trains.
zh: 但是当你看这个时，你在谈论失控列车。

speaker: Unknown
en: When you look at the national debt, though, it does look very much like a runaway train.
zh: 当你查看国债时，它确实看起来非常像一列失控列车。

speaker: Unknown
en: Want to know where inflation comes from?
zh: 想知道通货膨胀来自哪里吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: That's where inflation comes from.
zh: 那就是通货膨胀的来源。

speaker: Unknown
en: By printing more dollars to pay for that debt, which is what happens.
zh: 通过印更多的美元来偿还那些债务，这就是正在发生的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: The Federal Reserve buys the debt and they issue dollars to the bank system to buy the debt from the government.
zh: 美联储购买债务，他们向银行系统发行美元以从政府那里购买债务。

speaker: Unknown
en: Remember, the Federal Reserve is separate from the government.
zh: 记住，美联储是独立于政府的。

speaker: Unknown
en: The Federal Reserve can print dollars.
zh: 美联储可以印美元。

speaker: Unknown
en: They can send dollars to banks.
zh: 他们可以把美元发送给银行。

speaker: Unknown
en: And now the banks can loan money out and it makes its way into the economy.
zh: 现在银行可以把钱贷出去，钱就会进入经济体系。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now there's more dollars in the economy.
zh: 现在经济体系中有更多的美元。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that money was, you know, owed back to the government at some point.
zh: 那笔钱，你知道，在某个时候是需要偿还给政府的。

speaker: Unknown
en: But the Federal Reserve may never get paid back.
zh: 但美联储可能永远拿不回钱。

speaker: Unknown
en: They may just keep adding and adding and adding and adding.
zh: 他们可能只是不断地增加、增加、增加、增加。

speaker: Unknown
en: And they're just printing more and more dollars.
zh: 他们只是在印越来越多的美元。

speaker: Unknown
en: Is that sustainable?
zh: 那是可持续的吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: No.
zh: 不。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I don't understand the force that's going to intervene to stop this sort of compounding debt.
zh: 所以我不理解那种将要介入来阻止这种复合债务的力量。

speaker: Unknown
en: The outcome of this is socialism.
zh: 这的结局是社会主义。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's the moment we're in right now.
zh: 这就是我们此刻所处的时刻。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's why we're seeing this wave of socialism.
zh: 这就是为什么我们看到这股社会主义浪潮。

speaker: Unknown
en: I've been saying for five years, we're going to face a wave of socialism.
zh: 我这五年来一直在说，我们将面临一股社会主义浪潮。

speaker: Unknown
en: And after Donald Trump was elected, my prediction for the next year was that the next wave in politics in America will be socialism.
zh: 在唐纳德·特朗普当选后，我第二年的预测是，美国政治的下一波浪潮将是社会主义。

speaker: Unknown
en: And people thought I was crazy.
zh: 人们以为我疯了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I'm like, it is absolutely inevitable if you look at this.
zh: 而我就说，如果你看这个，这绝对是不可避免的。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is where we're headed.
zh: 这就是我们要去的地方。

speaker: Unknown
en: It is de facto socialism when the government employs roughly one half of the people of the United States.
zh: 当政府雇佣大约一半的美国人民时，这就是事实上的社会主义。

speaker: Unknown
en: Right now, if you look at all the federal, state, local agencies, so the people that are employed, the people that are contractors of those agencies, and then the people that live off of some sort of government pension or social security system, the total amount is close to 50% of Americans.
zh: 现在，如果你看所有的联邦、州和地方机构，所以那些被雇佣的人，那些这些机构的承包商，还有那些靠某种政府养老金或社会保障系统生活的人，总人数接近美国人的 50%。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we're getting to a point where people are like, the only place I can go is more money from the government.
zh: 所以我们正在到达这样一个地步，人们觉得，我唯一能去的地方就是从政府那里获得更多的钱。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then eventually the government becomes the whole economy.
zh: 然后最终政府成为了整个经济。

speaker: Unknown
en: If the outcome of socialism was to cause capitalism?
zh: 如果社会主义的结果是去导致资本主义？

speaker: Unknown
en: It's a great question.
zh: 这是一个很好的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it was capitalism plus policies.
zh: 我认为这是资本主义加上政策。

speaker: Unknown
en: Let's say you have a million dollars.
zh: 假设你有一百万美元。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're making, say, 10% a year.
zh: 你每年赚，比如说，10%。

speaker: Unknown
en: Next year, you have $1.1 million.
zh: 第二年，你有 110 万美元。

speaker: Unknown
en: The next year, you have $1.21 million or whatever, and you keep adding it up.
zh: 再下一年，你有 121 万美元或者随便多少钱，你不断地把它加起来。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's called compounding.
zh: 这叫复利。

speaker: Unknown
en: After a couple of years, your million dollars turns into $10 million.
zh: 几年后，你的一百万美元变成了一千万美元。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you never have to sell shares along the way.
zh: 而且你在此期间永远不必出售股票。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can just own the shares and whatever's going up.
zh: 你可以只持有股票以及任何正在上涨的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: Your value just keeps going up.
zh: 你的价值只是不断上升。

speaker: Unknown
en: You've never paid taxes along the way.
zh: 你从未在此过程中缴税。

speaker: Unknown
en: Boom, boom, boom, boom, boom.
zh: 轰，轰，轰，轰，轰。

speaker: Unknown
en: And suddenly, fast forward a couple of years, instead of having a million, you've now got 10.
zh: 突然间，快进几年，不再是拥有一百万，你现在有了 10。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's capital compounding over time.
zh: 那是资本随时间的复利。

speaker: Unknown
en: Meanwhile, if you're working, every paycheck, taxes are taken out.
zh: 与此同时，如果你在工作，每一份薪水，都会被扣除税款。

speaker: Unknown
en: Every time you get a check, every time you get more money, more capital, taxes are taken out.
zh: 每次你收到一张支票，每次你获得更多的钱，更多的资本，都会被扣除税款。

speaker: Unknown
en: So if you don't get capital, if you don't get enough savings to allow you to compound, you are never going to get there.
zh: 所以如果你没有资本，如果你没有足够的储蓄让你复利，你永远无法到达那里。

speaker: Unknown
en: So from a tax policy perspective, labor working for your money should have never been taxed higher than earning returns on your capital.
zh: 所以从税收政策的角度来看，为钱而工作的劳动，其税率永远不应该高于从资本中赚取回报。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you're saying tax the rich?
zh: 所以你是说向富人征税？

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm saying tax capital.
zh: 我是说向资本征税。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: at a rate that's equivalent to labor.
zh: 以等同于劳动的税率。

speaker: Unknown
en: Wealth taxes?
zh: 财富税？

speaker: Unknown
en: Wealth taxes are asset seizures.
zh: 财富税是资产没收。

speaker: Unknown
en: Definitely no.
zh: 绝对不行。

speaker: Unknown
en: So one of the principles of the United States and the principle of what this country was founded on is private property rights.
zh: 所以美国的原则之一，也是这个国家建立的原则之一，就是私有财产权。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you go back to England, right?
zh: 如果你回溯到英格兰，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: Like 500 years.
zh: 比如 500 年前。

speaker: Unknown
en: Or let's just talk Europe broadly.
zh: 或者我们就泛泛地谈谈欧洲。

speaker: Unknown
en: There were very few places where you as an individual citizen had rights to own private property.
zh: 很少有地方让你作为个人公民拥有拥有私有财产的权利。

speaker: Unknown
en: There were very few places where you could say, I have this thing and it doesn't belong to the king or it doesn't belong to whatever the local lord is.
zh: 很少有地方你能说，我拥有这个东西，它不属于国王，也不属于当地的任何领主。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like everything was the property of the lords, of the higher class, of the upper class.
zh: 所有的东西都是领主的、上层阶级的、上流社会的财产。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was endowed to them, it was vested to them by birthright.
zh: 它是授予给他们的，它是通过世袭权利赋予他们的。

speaker: Unknown
en: For centuries.
zh: 持续了几个世纪。

speaker: Unknown
en: Same in Asia, same in the Middle East, same in Africa.
zh: 亚洲也一样，中东也一样，非洲也一样。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, like every nation started out with the system where people didn't have rights to private property.
zh: 我的意思是，每个国家开始时都有这样一个人们没有私有财产权利的制度。

speaker: Unknown
en: Those who had kind of these systems above could decide who got what.
zh: 那些拥有这些上层体系的人可以决定谁得到什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: So the United States was founded on one of the principles of private property for an individual that, you know, I think when they were drafting the Declaration of Independence, it was about life, liberty, and the pursuit of property.
zh: 所以美国的建立是基于个人私有财产的原则之一，你知道，我认为当他们起草《独立宣言》时，那是关于生命、自由和追求财产。

speaker: Unknown
en: And they later changed it to pursuit of happiness.
zh: 后来他们把它改成了追求幸福。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the pursuit of property was really the measure of what you've accumulated as an individual.
zh: 追求财产实际上是你作为一个人积累了什么的衡量标准。

speaker: Unknown
en: You now have a right to accumulate things.
zh: 你现在有权积累东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: You now have a right to build value, to build wealth, to build a house and have your family in your house and have all these things.
zh: 你现在有权创造价值，创造财富，建造房子，让你的家人住进你的房子，拥有所有这些东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: That was the principle of the United States.
zh: 这就是美国的原则。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm all for taxes when people transact, when they turn their stock that they've held for a couple of years into cash and buy something with it.
zh: 我完全支持当人们交易时征税，当他们把持有了几年的股票变成现金并用它买东西时。

speaker: Unknown
en: Boom, tax.
zh: 轰，税。

speaker: Unknown
en: You get taxed on that.
zh: 你要为此纳税。

speaker: Unknown
en: If that's the right model, that's when you should get taxed.
zh: 如果那是正确的模式，那就是你应该被征税的时候。

speaker: Unknown
en: Right then, when you're able to turn that asset that you own into another asset.
zh: 就在那时，当你能够把你拥有的那项资产变成另一项资产。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that's what we do today.
zh: 这就是我们今天所做的。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's an income tax or a capital gains tax, like when you realize that gain.
zh: 那是所得税或资本利得税，就像当你实现那个收益时。

speaker: Unknown
en: But if I go into your shares and I'm like, hey, I'm going to take 5% of your shares, what are you losing?
zh: 但如果我进入你的股票份额，我说，嘿，我要拿走你 5% 的股份，你会失去什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, you can't use those shares to buy anything.
zh: 嗯，你不能用那些股份去买任何东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because as soon as you try and buy something, you owe tax on those shares.
zh: 因为一旦你试图买东西，你就欠那些股份的税。

speaker: Unknown
en: So by taking away your shares before you've actually transacted with them, before you've actually sold them, or taking away your private property, your home, or giving the government the right to come in your garage and audit everything you own and say, hey, this year we're doing a 2% tax.
zh: 所以通过在你实际交易它们之前，在你实际出售它们之前拿走你的股份，或者拿走你的私有财产，你的房子，或者给政府权利进入你的车库并审计你拥有的所有东西并说，嘿，今年我们要征收 2% 的税。

speaker: Unknown
en: That is antithetical to what the United States was founded on, which was a founding principle of private property.
zh: 这与美国的建国初衷背道而驰，其建国原则就是私有财产。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now, if your property goes up in value and then you eventually turn it into some other property, that's a transaction and that's when you get taxed.
zh: 现在，如果你的财产升值了，然后你最终把它变成了其他财产，那就是一笔交易，那时候你就被征税了。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's how the system's set up.
zh: 这就是系统的设置方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: So if we have an issue with people having too much wealth, that's the moment to increase the tax rate.
zh: 所以如果我们对人们拥有太多财富有问题，那就是增加税率的时刻。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's capital gains tax, income tax on high earners.
zh: 那是资本利得税，对高收入者的所得税。

speaker: Unknown
en: Those two things can get you 97% of the way there.
zh: 这两件事可以让你达到 97% 的目标。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you're not really going to gain much.
zh: 而且你真的不会获得多少。

speaker: Unknown
en: Separately, we can kind of talk about the numbers on this, but like tax the rich...
zh: 另外，我们可以稍微谈谈这里的数字，但比如向富人征税……

speaker: Unknown
en: all for it, but tax the rich when they transact, when they sell, when they have a capital gain, if they borrow against their assets.
zh: 完全支持，但在富人交易、出售、获得资本收益或抵押资产借款时向他们征税。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is another thing that's wrong about our system today.
zh: 这是当今制度中另一个错误的方面。

speaker: Unknown
en: If I'm very wealthy, I own a bunch of stock and I've never sold any of the stock.
zh: 如果我非常富有，我拥有一堆股票而且我从未出售过任何股票。

speaker: Unknown
en: If I borrow against my stock to go buy a yacht, I don't pay taxes.
zh: 如果我抵押我的股票去买游艇，我不需要缴税。

speaker: Unknown
en: that should be a taxable event.
zh: 那应该是一个应税事件。

speaker: Unknown
en: We should fix that.
zh: 我们应该修复这个问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's an easy fix in the tax system.
zh: 那是税收系统中的一个容易修复的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm not taking away your private property, but as soon as you borrow against that, it's effectively like transacting on that property.
zh: 我不是要拿走你的私有财产，但只要你抵押它，这实际上就像是在交易该财产。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that's a moment to pay a tax.
zh: 所以那是纳税的时刻。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if we think that the rich aren't paying enough taxes, you can raise income tax or capital gains taxes to get them to pay more.
zh: 如果我们认为富人缴税不够，你可以提高所得税或资本利得税来让他们多付钱。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is what I was going to say, but you arrived at it, was most people that own stock in big companies will just borrow against their stock, and they never pay a tax.
zh: 这正是我想说的，但你先提到了，就是拥有大公司股票的大多数人只会抵押他们的股票，而且他们从不缴税。

speaker: Unknown
en: I didn't know this until I was, I'm going to say 26, and my company had gone public, and this bank in Europe approached me and said, by the way, we'll give you 20% of whatever your, the value of the stock you have in my company called Social Chain AG is a tax-free loan.
zh: 我直到……我要说我 26 岁的时候才知道这个，当时我的公司已经上市了，欧洲的一家银行找到我说，顺便说一句，我们将给你……你在我名为 Social Chain AG 的公司中所拥有的股票价值的 20%，这是一笔免税贷款。

speaker: Unknown
en: I was like, explain this to me again.
zh: 我当时想，再给我解释一遍。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you'll just send me millions of pounds and I don't have to pay tax.
zh: 所以你会直接给我几百万英镑，而我不用缴税。

speaker: Unknown
en: You don't have to sell your shares.
zh: 你不必出售你的股份。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't have to sell anything.
zh: 我不必出售任何东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: I said, well, look at the rest of my portfolio.
zh: 我说，好吧，看看我投资组合的其余部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I had some Facebook stock at the time.
zh: 我当时持有一些 Facebook 股票。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're like, well, we'll give you 50% to 60% loan to value on that.
zh: 他们说，好吧，我们可以给你提供 50% 到 60% 的估值贷款。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you have a million dollars of Facebook stock, we will transfer you today 700 grand tax free.
zh: 如果你有一百万美元的 Facebook 股票，我们今天就会给你转账 70 万，免税。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I can do with that whatever I want.
zh: 我可以拿这笔钱做任何我想做的事。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I thought, fucking hell, this is what the rich do.
zh: 我想，天哪，这就是富人做的事。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's exactly right.
zh: 完全正确。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the truth is that no one talks about, behind closed doors, everyone knows that it needs to change.
zh: 事实是没人谈论这个，但在私下里，每个人都知道这需要改变。

speaker: Unknown
en: But no one wants to say it because...
zh: 但没人想说出来，因为……

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm saying it.
zh: 我在说它。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Gotta change.
zh: 必须改变。

speaker: Unknown
en: What's interesting about that is, say that I have 10 million of Facebook stock, and I take a loan, and they give me 5 million in cash.
zh: 有趣的是，假设我有一千万的 Facebook 股票，我借了一笔贷款，他们给了我五百万现金。

speaker: Unknown
en: What a rich person then does is they take that 5 million, and they go and buy other assets.
zh: 富人接下来做的是拿走那五百万，去买其他资产。

speaker: Unknown
en: Exactly right.
zh: 完全正确。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then they start acquiring more and more assets.
zh: 然后他们开始获取越来越多的资产。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's what's unfair about the system, because then when you have capital...
zh: 这就是系统不公平的地方，因为当你拥有资本时……

speaker: Unknown
en: You're accumulating more capital.
zh: 你正在积累更多的资本。

speaker: Unknown
en: While labor, if you haven't made that cross that chasm from labor to capital, you're still here grinding every month, grinding every week, trying to pay your frigging bills.
zh: 而对于劳动力，如果你还没有跨越从劳动力到资本的鸿沟，你仍然在这里每个月拼命工作，每个星期拼命工作，试图支付你该死的账单。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then these guys have all these shenanigans that are going on.
zh: 然后这些人有所有这些正在进行的鬼把戏。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: It is wrong and it needs to be fixed.
zh: 这是错的，需要被修复。

speaker: Unknown
en: The answer, though, is not taking private property.
zh: 然而，答案不是拿走私有财产。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: As soon as you start taking private property.
zh: 一旦你开始拿走私有财产。

speaker: Unknown
en: Those gates are open.
zh: 那些大门就打开了。

speaker: Unknown
en: By the way, it's not even going to be constitutional in the United States.
zh: 顺便说一句，这在美国甚至不会是合宪的。

speaker: Unknown
en: The Fifth Amendment has this taker clause.
zh: 第五修正案有这个征收条款。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, it's not it's legally like not going to win in federal court.
zh: 你知道，这在法律上像是不可能胜诉的。

speaker: Unknown
en: It could work in some states, some states.
zh: 这在某些州可能行得通，某些州。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's seven states that actually have a constitutional ban on private property tax like this.
zh: 实际上有七个州确实拥有针对此类私人财产税的宪法禁令。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's, you know, 43 states where it's game on.
zh: 还有，你知道，有 43 个州，那里是游戏开始。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we'll see how they play out in the courts as they try to pass these wealth taxes as well.
zh: 我们将看看它们在法庭上如何演变，当它们试图通过这些财富税的时候。

speaker: Unknown
en: But these are asset seizure taxes.
zh: 但这些是资产没收税。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can have a wealth tax by raising capital gains.
zh: 你可以通过提高资本利得来征收财富税。

speaker: Unknown
en: make high income or high asset people pay more taxes or whatever, when they sell stuff or when they buy stuff.
zh: 让高收入或高资产的人缴纳更多税款或者随便什么，当他们卖东西或者买东西的时候。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's a lot of ways to tax wealth.
zh: 有很多方法可以对财富征税。

speaker: Unknown
en: But taking assets from people after they've paid their taxes or before they've paid their taxes is not the right way to do it.
zh: 但是在人们交税之后或交税之前从他们手中拿走资产不是做这件事的正确方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: What will ultimately happen?
zh: 最终会发生什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: So the ultimate outcome will be that 51% of people will say, hey, give me all the stuff that the 49% have.
zh: 所以最终的结果将是 51% 的人会说，嘿，给我那 49% 的人拥有的所有东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: What would stop them from doing that?
zh: 什么会阻止他们那样做？

speaker: Unknown
en: Because ultimately, you can take as much as you want from a minority of people and distribute it to the majority.
zh: 因为最终，你可以从少数人那里拿走你想要的任何东西，然后分配给大多数人。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that minority starts out with a few billionaires, then a couple more 50 millionaires, then a couple more 10 millionaires, then millionaires, then 100,000aires.
zh: 那个少数群体开始于几个亿万富翁，然后是更多的 5000 万富翁，然后是更多的 1000 万富翁，然后是百万富翁，然后是 10 万富翁。

speaker: Unknown
en: And there's no limit to where this thing goes.
zh: 而且这件事发展到哪里是没有限制的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that is socialism.
zh: 这就是社会主义。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And what does that do in terms of how talent moves and how people move to different places?
zh: 在人才如何流动以及人们如何搬到不同地方方面，这会产生什么影响？

speaker: Unknown
en: I know billionaires.
zh: 我认识亿万富翁。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Many of them have moved or are planning to move out of California, just on the thread of this.
zh: 他们中的许多人已经搬走或正计划搬出加州，仅仅是因为这一点的话题。

speaker: Unknown
en: And people say, F them, good riddance, get rid of them.
zh: 人们会说，去他们的，滚得好，摆脱他们。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, the top 1% of taxpayers in California pay the majority of taxes in the state.
zh: 你知道，加州前 1% 的纳税人缴纳了该州大部分的税款。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it's probably, it's definitely north of 40%, but it's probably the majority.
zh: 我认为大概是，肯定超过 40%，但可能是大多数。

speaker: Unknown
en: The top 1% of earners pay 40 to 50% of California's total personal income tax, depending on stock market capital gains performance.
zh: 收入最高的 1% 的人支付了加州个人所得税总额的 40% 到 50%，取决于股票市场资本收益的表现。

speaker: Unknown
en: There you go.
zh: 就是那样。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that 1% are the people I'm talking about that are leaving the state because they see where this is headed.
zh: 所以这 1% 的人就是我说的那些正在离开该州的人，因为他们看到了这事的走向。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't think California wants that.
zh: 我不认为加州希望那样。

speaker: Unknown
en: Those are very productive people for the state.
zh: 那些对该州来说是非常富有生产力的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're people that create...
zh: 他们是创造……的人

speaker: Unknown
en: Companies that hire people that pay well, go to fancy restaurants, pay for cars.
zh: 雇佣高薪人员的公司，去高档餐厅，买车。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, they support the economy.
zh: 我是说，他们支撑着经济。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's not just the taxes, but they're a big part of capital flowing through the economy.
zh: 不仅仅是税收，他们是经济中流动的资本的重要组成部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: We saw this happen in France.
zh: 我们看到这在法国发生了。

en: I think this, like, event...

speaker: Unknown
en: But the pace of disruption here seems to be different than like the industrial revolution.
zh: 但这里的颠覆速度似乎不同于工业革命。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's targeting cognitive work.
zh: 它针对的是认知工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's built on this platform called the internet, which has this.
zh: 它是建立在这个称为互联网的平台之上的，它具有这个。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm telling you, I just don't see it.
zh: 我告诉你，我只是看不到它。

speaker: Unknown
en: I like at my work, everyone's using AI and everyone's just doing more.
zh: 我喜欢我的工作，每个人都在用 AI，每个人只是在做得更多。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then they ask for more employees.
zh: 然后他们要求更多员工。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can kind of think about a business having two sides.
zh: 你可以某种程度上考虑一个生意有两个方面。

speaker: Unknown
en: Revenue and costs.
zh: 收入和成本。

speaker: Unknown
en: Revenue is I'm making stuff and people are paying me for the things I'm making or doing.
zh: 收入就是我在制造东西，人们为我制造或做的事情付钱给我。

speaker: Unknown
en: Cost is how am I operating the business?
zh: 成本就是我如何经营生意？

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, what am I spending?
zh: 像，我在花什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: And the argument has always been like, okay, you're going to lose customer service reps. You're going to lose all the cost side of the equation.
zh: 而论证一直就像，好吧，你会失去客服代表。你会失去等式所有的成本端。

speaker: Unknown
en: No one ever says you're going to lose the revenue side.
zh: 没有人说过你会失去收入端。

speaker: Unknown
en: The truth is on the revenue side, what ends up happening is you create new products that you couldn't create before because of AI.
zh: 真相是在收入端，最终发生的是你创造了以前无法创造的新产品，因为有了 AI。

speaker: Unknown
en: The technology enables so much advancement in your business.
zh: 该技术在你的生意中实现了如此多的进步。

speaker: Unknown
en: Let's say you're a material science company.
zh: 假设你是一家材料科学公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is totally esoteric, but like, let's say your job as a company is to discover new materials, new synthetics that can be used to make microchips or be used for computing or be used for travel or for airplanes.
zh: 这完全是很深奥的，但像，假设你作为公司的工作是发现新材料、新的合成物，可以用来制造微芯片，或用于计算，或用于旅行，或用于飞机。

speaker: Unknown
en: The material science world.
zh: 材料科学世界。

speaker: Unknown
en: has been challenged by its experimental cycle.
zh: 一直受到其实验周期的挑战。

speaker: Unknown
en: You got to create an experiment, make a product, test it, do it all manually.
zh: 你得创建一个实验，制造一个产品，测试它，全部手动完成。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's all creative ideas.
zh: 这都是创造性的想法。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's all human potential.
zh: 这都是人类潜能。

speaker: Unknown
en: AI can now screen through millions of material science ideas in a computer, print them out, test them, and you can automate that throughput.
zh: AI 现在可以在计算机中筛选数百万个材料科学想法，把它们打印出来，测试它们，你可以自动化那个吞吐量。

speaker: Unknown
en: Therefore, that materials company can now have more revenue.
zh: 因此，那家材料公司现在可以有更多收入。

speaker: Unknown
en: They can make more products.
zh: 他们可以制造更多产品。

speaker: Unknown
en: Do you not think that maybe there's a possibility that people like me and you exist in this particular band?
zh: 你不认为也许存在一种可能性，即像你我这样的人存在于这个特定波段中？

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, because we're both founders and we have capital, and we're thinking about how to really push intelligence to create new things, that maybe we, because what you're saying I can relate to, I can relate to the fact that AI has made me actually quite, it's probably made me more ambitious about hiring, especially in the near term.
zh: 嗯，因为我们都是创始人，而且我们有资本，我们在思考如何真正推动智能来创造新事物，也许我们，因为你说的我能感同身受，我能感同身受的是 AI 实际上让我变得相当……它可能让我在招聘方面更有雄心，尤其是在短期内。

speaker: Unknown
en: I would caveat it by saying that there's a certain type of role that I'm now hiring much less, right?
zh: 我会补充一点说，我现在招聘得少得多的某种特定类型的角色，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: And especially when you think about entry-level roles, I have to pause a lot more now because a lot of the agents and some tooling can do some of those things that I would have otherwise hired for.
zh: 特别是当你考虑到初级角色时，我现在不得不更多地停顿，因为很多智能体和一些工具可以做我原本会招聘人来做的一些事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: But generally, I feel like I'm hiring as fast as I possibly can.
zh: 但总的来说，我觉得我正在尽可能快地招聘。

speaker: Unknown
en: But would you not say that for like the 21-year-old that's graduated from university or the DoorDash driver...
zh: 但你不会说对于那些……比如 21 岁刚大学毕业的人或者是 DoorDash 司机……

speaker: Unknown
en: or those types of individuals, where the leap from where they currently are on a factory floor assembling a part or flipping packages, the leap from where they are to this new world is so great that there's going to be this messy middle.
zh: 或者那些类型的个人，他们从目前在工厂车间组装零件或翻转包裹的地方，跨越到这个新世界的距离是如此之大，以至于将会出现这种混乱的中间地带。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, what I'm saying is as new products are created, new revenue comes in, you don't cut costs, you grow costs.
zh: 是的，我要说的是，随着新产品被创造出来，新收入进来，你不会削减成本，你会增加成本。

speaker: Unknown
en: and you hire more people, and you up-level, and you train people.
zh: 并且你雇佣更多人，你提升层级，你培训人们。

speaker: Unknown
en: That is what I'm seeing on the ground.
zh: 这是我在实地看到的。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, we just published, I think, one of the lowest unemployment rates in the U.S. And I think that this idea...
zh: 你知道，我们刚刚发布了，我认为，美国历史上最低的失业率之一。我认为这种想法……

speaker: Unknown
en: that your current job is going to get disrupted and you're going to lose your job, I don't think it's how the enterprise transitions.
zh: 即你目前的工作将被颠覆，你会失去你的工作，我认为这不是企业转型的方向。

speaker: Unknown
en: The enterprise transitions, meaning companies, by doing more things and bringing people up the ladder, hiring more people.
zh: 企业的转型，即公司，通过做更多事情并把人带上阶梯，雇佣更多人。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's just what I'm seeing on the ground.
zh: 而这正是我在实地看到的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think that there's a media narrative on like, oh my God, there was a layoff at so-and-so company because it underlines what they've been promoting to everyone, which is AI is going to cause job loss.
zh: 我认为有一种媒体叙事就像，天哪，某某公司发生了裁员，因为它强调了他们一直向每个人兜售的观点，即 AI 将导致失业。

speaker: Unknown
en: The interesting thing is it didn't come from the media.
zh: 有趣的是，它并非来自媒体。

speaker: Unknown
en: It came from the AI guys.
zh: 它来自 AI 伙计们。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is the biggest crazy thing.
zh: 这是最大的疯狂之事。

speaker: Unknown
en: This drives me nuts.
zh: 这让我发疯。

speaker: Unknown
en: I listen to All In podcast.
zh: 我听 All In 播客。

speaker: Unknown
en: By the way, it's one of my favorite podcasts.
zh: 顺便说一句，这是我最喜欢的播客之一。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't think I've ever missed an episode.
zh: 我认为我从未错过一期。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I very much understand your perspective and all of your colleagues.
zh: 所以我非常理解你的观点以及你所有的同事。

speaker: Unknown
en: I had no idea you were a fan.
zh: 我不知道你是粉丝。

speaker: Unknown
en: No, no, I do.
zh: 不，不，我是。

speaker: Unknown
en: I've listened to it.
zh: 我听过。

speaker: Unknown
en: I've gone on people's shows where they're like, I don't know who you are.
zh: 我上过人们的节目，他们就像，我不知道你是谁。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I'm like, it's good to meet you.
zh: 我就像，很高兴见到你。

speaker: Unknown
en: No, no, no.
zh: 不，不，不。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't think I've ever missed an episode since the beginning.
zh: 我认为从开始以来我从未错过一期。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I understand your perspective.
zh: 所以我理解你的观点。

speaker: Unknown
en: You've heard all this.
zh: 你听过所有这些。

speaker: Unknown
en: I've heard all of this and I've heard Jason's opinion.
zh: 我听过所有这些，我也听过 Jason 的观点。

speaker: Unknown
en: Weirdly, I tend to side a little bit more with Jason on this.
zh: 奇怪的是，在这点上我有点更倾向于 Jason。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because I think Jason, I don't know why his arguments seem to present the most nuance.
zh: 因为我认为 Jason，我不知道为什么他的论点似乎呈现出最细微的差别。

speaker: Unknown
en: And also, I would say, when we think about different people's incentives, yeah, you're right.
zh: 而且，我想说，当我们考虑不同人的动机时，是的，你是对的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Often on that show, it's framed as a media narrative.
zh: 在那个节目上，它经常被构建为一种媒体叙事。

speaker: Unknown
en: Whereas it's actually all your friends.
zh: 而实际上这全是你的朋友们。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, no.
zh: 是的，不。

speaker: Unknown
en: So first of all, none of them are my friends.
zh: 所以首先，他们中没有一个是我的朋友。

speaker: Unknown
en: Elon's your friend.
zh: Elon 是你的朋友。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay.
zh: 好的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So what I will say, like I've said this on the show, I'll say it again.
zh: 所以我想说，就像我在节目上说过的那样，我会再说一遍。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think there is a deep arrogance in making these sorts of proclamations.
zh: 我认为在发表这类声明时存在一种深刻的傲慢。

speaker: Unknown
en: Which proclamations?
zh: 哪些声明？

speaker: Unknown
en: That we're not going to work anymore.
zh: 我们不再工作了。

speaker: Unknown
en: It effectively discounts the human.
zh: 这实际上贬低了人类。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's like what you do today is your limit.
zh: 这就像你今天做的事情就是你的极限。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I think that this idea that like these jobs will go away is sourced by people that are seeing the crazy stuff that they're doing.
zh: 但我认为这些工作将消失的想法，来源于那些看到了他们正在做的疯狂事情的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: And they're like, oh, my God, this is amazing.
zh: 然后他们会说，噢，我的天，这太棒了。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm responsible for this.
zh: 我对此负责。

speaker: Unknown
en: We are going to change the world.
zh: 我们要改变世界。

speaker: Unknown
en: We are going to take all jobs and they're all going to sit in my computer.
zh: 我们要接管所有工作，它们都将坐在我的电脑里。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't think that that's what happens because I think that humans have a profound capacity for doing things that, you know, these technologists don't necessarily see.
zh: 我不认为会发生这种情况，因为我认为人类有做事的深刻能力，你知道，这些技术人员并不一定看得到。

speaker: Unknown
en: The great technologists see technology.
zh: 伟大的技术人员看到技术。

speaker: Unknown
en: They don't see people.
zh: 他们看不到人。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think you have to see people, meaning the potential of people, of individuals.
zh: 我认为你必须看到人，意味着人的潜力，个体的潜力。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you have to believe in that.
zh: 你必须相信这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: They believe in technology, they engineer technology.
zh: 他们相信技术，他们设计技术。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I am not going to be pessimistic about people.
zh: 但我不会对人持悲观态度。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think that people have capacity in any environment.
zh: 我认为人在任何环境中都有能力。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, the amazing thing about humans is our adaptability.
zh: 我的意思是，人类令人惊叹的事情是我们的适应性。

speaker: Unknown
en: We can live in any climate.
zh: 我们可以在任何气候下生活。

speaker: Unknown
en: We can eat any kind of food.
zh: 我们可以吃任何种类的食物。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, we can work all these different jobs.
zh: 我的意思是，我们可以做所有这些不同的工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, we're amazing.
zh: 我的意思是，我们很棒。

speaker: Unknown
en: Humans are amazing.
zh: 人类很棒。

speaker: Unknown
en: And...
zh: 而且……

speaker: Unknown
en: Arguably, many humans have been limited in their potential.
zh: 可以说，许多人类的潜力一直受到限制。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think that AI enables more capacity for those individuals to realize more of their potential.
zh: 我认为 AI 为这些个体提供了更多能力以实现他们更多的潜力。

speaker: Unknown
en: Much of the conversation we've had about the US economy has centered around incentive structures leading to inevitable outcomes.
zh: 我们关于美国经济的大部分谈话都集中在导致不可避免结果的激励结构上。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, the older I've gotten, the more I just try and look at incentives to figure out behavior and also to figure out who to trust.
zh: 你知道，随着我年纪越大，我就越是试着通过看激励来搞清楚行为，也搞清楚该信任谁。

speaker: Unknown
en: So when I look at the incentives of the people that are building the AI companies, Andy Jassy has said that there's going to be fewer people doing some of the jobs that are being done today.
zh: 所以当我看那些建立 AI 公司的人的激励时，安迪·贾西说过，今天正在做的某些工作将会有更少的人去做。

speaker: Unknown
en: Then they cut, you know, tens of thousands of jobs.
zh: 然后他们裁掉了，你知道，数万个工作岗位。

speaker: Unknown
en: Mark Benioff, who I know has been on your show, cut 4,000 jobs and said, I need less heads because of AI.
zh: 马克·贝尼奥夫，我知道他在你的节目上，裁掉了 4000 个工作岗位并说，因为 AI，我需要更少的人手。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I swear, okay, maybe they're saying that because they want their share price to go up because it's a good, you know, we're going to reduce costs as a good narrative.
zh: 我发誓，好吧，也许他们这么说是因为他们想让股价上涨，因为这是一个很好的，你知道，我们要降低成本作为一个好的叙事。

speaker: Unknown
en: But then I look at the other, the AI CEOs, Dario, Elon, Sam Altman, and I go, their incentives, I'd say other than the exception of Elon, have just kind of changed with whatever's good for them at that moment.
zh: 然后我看其他人，AI CEO 们，达里奥、伊隆、萨姆·奥特曼，我想，除了伊隆是个例外，他们的激励基本上都随着那一刻对他们有利的东西而改变。

speaker: Unknown
en: Oftentimes, I actually, I think Dario might be the exception a little bit because he seems to be a bit more nuanced.
zh: 通常情况下，其实，我认为达里奥可能有点例外，因为他看起来更微妙一些。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: If I go back through the quotes of these individuals, you have Sam Altman in February 2015 saying, development of super machine intelligence is probably the greatest threat to the continued existence of humanity.
zh: 如果我回顾这些人的语录，萨姆·奥特曼在 2015 年 2 月说，超级机器智能的开发可能是人类持续生存的最大威胁。

speaker: Unknown
en: You have Elon in 2014 saying, with artificial intelligence, we are summoning the demon.
zh: 你有伊隆在 2014 年说，有了人工智能，我们正在召唤恶魔。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's far more dangerous than nukes.
zh: 它比核武器危险得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: Mitigating the risk of extinction from AI should be a global priority alongside societal scale risks such as pandemics and nuclear wars.
zh: 减轻来自 AI 的灭绝风险应与流行病和核战争等社会规模风险一起成为全球优先事项。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that was signed by Salm Altman, Demis, Dario, Bill Gates, amongst many hundreds of others.
zh: 这是由萨尔姆·奥特曼、德米斯、达里奥、比尔·盖茨以及其他数百人签署的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Salm Altman in the Senate in 2023.
zh: 萨尔姆·奥特曼 2023 年在参议院。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think if this technology goes wrong, it can go very wrong.
zh: 我认为如果这项技术出问题，它可能会出大问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: OpenAI, superintelligence letter they wrote.
zh: OpenAI，他们写的超级智能信件。

speaker: Unknown
en: The disempowerment of humanity or even human extinction could be caused by superintelligence.
zh: 人类权力的丧失甚至人类灭绝可能由超级智能引起。

speaker: Unknown
en: Again, in The Athletic, Sam Altman.
zh: 同样，在《竞技报》，萨姆·奥特曼。

speaker: Unknown
en: Jobs are definitely going to go away.
zh: 工作肯定会消失。

speaker: Unknown
en: Full stop.
zh: 句号。

speaker: Unknown
en: Dari Amadei, May 2025, he predicted a white-collar bloodbath, half of entry-level, white-collar jobs gone, unemployment at 10% to 20% within one to five years.
zh: 达里·阿马代，2025 年 5 月，他预测了一场白领大屠杀，一半的入门级白领工作消失，一到五年内失业率达到 10% 到 20%。

speaker: Unknown
en: 10% to 20% unemployment in one to five years.
zh: 一到五年内 10% 到 20% 的失业率。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's pretty high.
zh: 这相当高。

speaker: Unknown
en: And Altman at the Federal Reserve in July 2025 said, whole job categories will disappear.
zh: 而且 Altman 在 2025 年 7 月的美联储说，整个工作类别将会消失。

speaker: Unknown
en: Customer support first.
zh: 首先是客户支持。

speaker: Unknown
en: That one is, quote, totally, totally gone.
zh: 那一个是，引用，彻底，彻底消失了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then suddenly the message changed.
zh: 然后突然信息变了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Before his sort of pre-IPO discussions, he said things could go pretty wrong.
zh: 在他那种 IPO 前的讨论之前，他说事情可能会出大错。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then he says that he now has changed his mind and he's delighted that he feels like he was wrong.
zh: 然后说他现在已经改变了主意，他很高兴他觉得自己错了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And suddenly he's talking about how OpenAI and ChatGPT will benefit all of humanity.
zh: 突然他在谈论 OpenAI 和 ChatGPT 将如何造福全人类。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's their goal.
zh: 那是他们的目标。

speaker: Unknown
en: Should we trust the same people that told us to be scared when they say, don't be scared?
zh: 当他们说，别害怕时，我们应该相信那些告诉我们去害怕的同样的人吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: First of all, I think there was a bunch of companies that said early on,
zh: 首先，我认为有一堆公司很早之前就说，

speaker: Unknown
en: that they were like cutting all their customer service reps, which was the big company starts with a K. Klaner, but I did call the founder.
zh: 他们像是在裁掉所有的客服代表，那是家大公司名字以 K 开头。Klaner，但我确实给创始人打了电话。

speaker: Unknown
en: And what'd you find out?
zh: 你发现了什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: He said that he's been misinterpreted in the press.
zh: 他说他在媒体上被误解了。

speaker: Unknown
en: I heard you guys talk about this in the All In podcast, but I've actually called him live on this show.
zh: 我在 All In 播客里听到你们谈论这个，但我实际上在这个节目里现场给他打过电话。

speaker: Unknown
en: And did he rehire or like, what did he do?
zh: 他重新雇佣了吗或者像，他做了什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: He said that the media just completely misconstrued what he said.
zh: 他说媒体完全歪曲了他所说的话。

speaker: Unknown
en: He said he had 7,000 employees.
zh: 他说他有 7,000 名员工。

speaker: Unknown
en: By the end of last summer, he said he'd be on 3,000, but the media framed it as I had 7,000 employees and then I tried to cut some, I realized I couldn't and I went back, that's not what happened.
zh: 到去年夏天结束时，他说他会减少到 3,000 人，但媒体把它描述成我有 7,000 名员工然后我试图裁掉一些，我意识到我不能然后我又回去了，那不是发生的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's just, I see it on all these podcasts, I'm just repeating it.
zh: 只是，我在所有这些播客上看到它，我只是在重复它。

speaker: Unknown
en: I heard it repeated on your show, like...
zh: 我在你们的节目上听到它被重复，像……

speaker: Unknown
en: But he said, we are cutting because of AI.
zh: 但他说，我们因为 AI 而在裁员。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.

speaker: Unknown
en: But by taking their assets, even if you took 100% of the billionaire's assets, that's one year of spending.
zh: 但是通过拿走他们的资产，即使你拿走亿万富翁资产的100%，那也只是一年的开支。

speaker: Unknown
en: It doesn't actually solve a fiscal problem.
zh: 这实际上并不能解决财政问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: The tax rate is the fiscal problem.
zh: 税率是财政问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: So for these people, the 63% that are potentially championing socialism because they need a solution, and it sounds like a solution, make my bills cheaper.
zh: 所以对于这些人，那潜在的63%支持社会主义的人，因为他们需要一个解决方案，而这听起来像个解决方案，让我的账单更便宜。

speaker: Unknown
en: What they don't hear from other politicians is a better solution, and this one sounds great.
zh: 他们从其他政客那里听不到的是更好的解决方案，而这个听起来很棒。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is what's crazy to me.
zh: 这对我来说太疯狂了。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't get why all the politicians are fighting against a wealth tax or for a wealth tax when there's literally 15 other things you could do to make this better.
zh: 我不明白为什么所有政客都在反对财富税或支持财富税，而实际上你可以做15件其他事情来让情况变好。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, this is crazy.
zh: 比如，这太疯狂了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Make the capital gains and income tax the same.
zh: 让资本利得和所得税一样。

speaker: Unknown
en: Cut stupid spending at the federal level.
zh: 削减联邦层面的愚蠢开支。

speaker: Unknown
en: And all of a sudden, things become more affordable.
zh: 突然间，一切都变得更容易负担了。

speaker: Unknown
en: People have more take-home pay.
zh: 人们有更多的到手工资。

speaker: Unknown
en: They can afford more stuff.
zh: 他们能负担更多的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: But let's be honest.
zh: 但让我们诚实一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're not going to be able to cut the spending at the federal level.
zh: 你将无法削减联邦层面的开支。

speaker: Unknown
en: They've tried that.
zh: 他们试过那个。

speaker: Unknown
en: And because of this whole thing we just talked about, the four-year election cycles, Elon went in, he tried to cut it.
zh: 而且因为我们刚才谈论的整个事情，四年选举周期，Elon 进去了，他试图削减它。

speaker: Unknown
en: He bounced straight back out.
zh: 他直接又弹出来了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think that that to me was the most depressing piece because I was like, oh, my God, Elon's going to go in.
zh: 我认为那对我来说是最令人沮丧的部分，因为我是说，天哪，Elon 要进去了。

speaker: Unknown
en: He's going to blow up spending.
zh: 他要炸毁开支。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're finally going to cut all the nonsense out of the spending.
zh: 我们终于要把开支中所有的废话都剔除掉。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if Elon can't, no human can.
zh: 如果 Elon 都做不到，没有人能做到。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then I went and visited D.C. and I went to all these Congress meetings and sat with senators and I was like, oh, my God, none of them want to cut it.
zh: 然后我去参观了 D.C.，我去了所有这些国会会议，和参议员坐在一起，我想，天哪，他们中没有人想削减它。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like they're all on board with it.
zh: 就像他们都对此表示赞同。

speaker: Unknown
en: This isn't even a party thing.
zh: 这甚至不是党派的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is like everyone's doing it.
zh: 这就像是每个人都在这样做。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I'm like, this is the system.
zh: 我想，这就是系统。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is how it's set up.
zh: 这就是它的设置方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: Holy shit.
zh: 见鬼。

speaker: Unknown
en: We've had, Brian, a slightly change of direction, but linked to AI.
zh: 我们经历了一个稍微的改变方向，Brian，但与 AI 相关联。

speaker: Unknown
en: I know you work in the life sciences.
zh: 我知道你在生命科学领域工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I wanted to ask you, do you think we're going to be able to live forever soon or at least extend life significantly within the next couple of decades?
zh: 所以我想问你，你认为我们很快就能永远活着吗，或者至少在未来几十年内显著延长寿命？

speaker: Unknown
en: I do.
zh: 我认为会。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think the reason is we've discovered the mechanism of aging, which is the most fundamental of human diseases.
zh: 我认为原因是我们发现了衰老的机制，这是人类最根本的疾病。

speaker: Unknown
en: We have 10 trillion cells in our body.
zh: 我们身体里有10万亿个细胞。

speaker: Unknown
en: Every one of those cells has a copy of our DNA.
zh: 每一个细胞都有我们 DNA 的副本。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: in the nucleus of the cell.
zh: 在细胞核里。

speaker: Unknown
en: That DNA, segments of it, are called a gene.
zh: 那些 DNA，它的片段，被称为基因。

speaker: Unknown
en: A, C, T, and G make up the little nucleotides, and you put a bunch of them together, and that's a gene.
zh: A、C、T 和 G 组成了小核苷酸，你把一堆它们放在一起，那就是一个基因。

speaker: Unknown
en: What is a gene?
zh: 什么是基因？

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, a copy of that comes over to a protein printer in the cell called the ribosome, and the A, C, T, and G is the programming for which of 20 amino acids, three letters is one amino acid, that ribosome takes a segment of the DNA, copied as RNA, and it prints out...
zh: 好的，那个副本会来到细胞中一个叫做核糖体的蛋白质打印机里，A、C、T 和 G 是 20 种氨基酸中哪一种的编程，三个字母就是一个氨基酸，那个核糖体取一段 DNA，被复制成 RNA，然后它打印出……

speaker: Unknown
en: amino acids and a sequence of amino acids from that gene which is defined by that gene makes a protein so all a protein is is a is a chain of amino acids
zh: 氨基酸，以及来自那个基因的氨基酸序列，该序列由那个基因定义，从而制造出蛋白质，所以所有蛋白质仅仅是一个是一个氨基酸链

speaker: Unknown
en: As soon as it's done printing, those amino acids collapse into a three-dimensional machine called a protein.
zh: 一旦它打印完成，那些氨基酸就会坍缩成一个叫做蛋白质的三维机器。

speaker: Unknown
en: So proteins are three-dimensional machines, and they do crazy shit.
zh: 所以蛋白质是三维机器，它们做着疯狂的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like there is a protein in your mitochondria that spins 6,000 times a second as hydrogen protons go through it, and that's what makes energy in your cells.
zh: 比如你的线粒体里有一种蛋白质，当氢质子穿过它时，它每秒旋转 6000 次，这就是制造你细胞能量的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's what makes ATP.
zh: 那就是制造 ATP 的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's literally like a propeller, like a turbine in your mitochondria and your cell.
zh: 它实际上就像一个螺旋桨，就像你线粒体和细胞里的一个涡轮机。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's an incredible machine.
zh: 这是一个不可思议的机器。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's machines that carry oxygen.
zh: 有携带氧气的机器。

speaker: Unknown
en: from your lungs into your cells in your body to give them oxygen that they need to work.
zh: 从你的肺部进入你身体里的细胞，给它们工作所需的氧气。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, there are proteins that do all sorts of crazy stuff.
zh: 我的意思是，有各种各样的蛋白质做着各种疯狂的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: So all the genes are, are the programming for making proteins in your cell.
zh: 所以所有的基因仅仅是，是制造你细胞中蛋白质的编程。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now, your DNA is not a strand like this.
zh: 现在，你的 DNA 并不是像这样的一条链。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's actually kind of a small clustered thing.
zh: 它实际上是一种有点小的聚集成团的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And there are little molecules that sit on top of the DNA.
zh: 有一些小分子位于 DNA 之上。

speaker: Unknown
en: that turn a gene on or off.
zh: 它们开启或关闭基因。

speaker: Unknown
en: So if the molecule is sitting on top of a certain gene, that gene is off.
zh: 所以如果分子位于某个基因之上，那个基因就是关闭的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like a little switch?
zh: 像一个小开关？

speaker: Unknown
en: Like a switch.
zh: 就像一个开关。

speaker: Unknown
en: What's it called?
zh: 它叫什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: Someone used the name before.
zh: 之前有人用过这个名字。

speaker: Unknown
en: Histones.
zh: 组蛋白。

speaker: Unknown
en: Histones, okay.
zh: 组蛋白，好的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Or acetyl markers.
zh: 或者乙酰标记。

speaker: Unknown
en: I thought it was epigenetics, but maybe I'll...
zh: 我以为是表观遗传学，但我也许会……

speaker: Unknown
en: So this is all epigenetics.
zh: 所以这都是表观遗传学。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay.
zh: 好的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So for a given cell, there are genes that are on or off.
zh: 所以对于一个给定的细胞，有开启或关闭的基因。

speaker: Unknown
en: The genes that are on, those proteins are being made in that cell.
zh: 开启的基因，那些蛋白质正在那个细胞中被制造。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the genes that are off...
zh: 而关闭的基因……

speaker: Unknown
en: Those proteins are not being made in that cell.
zh: 那些蛋白质没有在那个细胞中被制造。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's what makes all of our cells in our body different.
zh: 这就是让我们身体里所有细胞变得不同的原因。

speaker: Unknown
en: Every one of our cells has the same DNA, but our eye cell and our brain cell and our heart cell and our skin cell just have different genes that are on or off.
zh: 我们每个细胞都有相同的 DNA，但我们的眼细胞、脑细胞、心肌细胞和皮肤细胞只是有不同的基因处于开启或关闭状态。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay, so those markers that sit on the genes, those little switches, every time you drink a glass of alcohol or you go in the sun and get hit by the sunlight or smoke a cigarette or eat some bad food that's burnt, all of these things can cut DNA.
zh: 好的，所以那些位于基因上的标记，那些小开关，每当你喝一杯酒，或者你去阳光下被阳光照射，或者抽一支烟，或者吃一些烧焦的不好的食物，所有这些事情都可能会切断 DNA。

speaker: Unknown
en: And when DNA gets cut, your cell is really good at fixing it.
zh: 当 DNA 被切断时，你的细胞非常擅长修复它。

speaker: Unknown
en: Puts it right back together.
zh: 把它直接拼回原样。

speaker: Unknown
en: Happening millions of times a second in your body.
zh: 在你身体里每秒发生数百万次。

speaker: Unknown
en: Literally all over your body.
zh: 实际上遍布你的全身。

speaker: Unknown
en: And your DNA is breaking and your cell is fixing it.
zh: 你的 DNA 正在断裂，而你的细胞正在修复它。

speaker: Unknown
en: But every time your cell fixes it, there's a chance that that switch moves a little bit.
zh: 但每次你的细胞修复它时，那个开关都有可能会移动一点点。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if the switch moves to the wrong place, suddenly that cell starts making the wrong protein or stops making the right protein.
zh: 如果开关移动到了错误的地方，突然那个细胞就开始制造错误的蛋白质，或者停止制造正确的蛋白质。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay.
zh: 好的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So statistically, over time, when you're a baby, everything is tuned great, working right.
zh: 所以从统计学上讲，随着时间的推移，当你是个婴儿时，一切都调优得很好，运作正常。

speaker: Unknown
en: All the right proteins are being made in every cell.
zh: 所有正确的蛋白质都在每个细胞中被制造。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're young.
zh: 你很年轻。

speaker: Unknown
en: Your skin is not wrinkly.
zh: 你的皮肤没有皱纹。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can run.
zh: 你能跑。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can breathe.
zh: 你能呼吸。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can see perfectly.
zh: 你能看得完美。

speaker: Unknown
en: As you're a young person, suddenly you turn 30.
zh: 当你是个年轻人时，突然你到了 30 岁。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you're like, wait, my vision's kind of fading a little bit.
zh: 然后你会想，等等，我的视力有点模糊了。

speaker: Unknown
en: I can't run as fast.
zh: 我跑不了那么快了。

speaker: Unknown
en: I can't breathe as deep.
zh: 我呼吸没那么深了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Oh my God, I'm getting wrinkles around my eyes.
zh: 天哪，我眼睛周围长皱纹了。

speaker: Unknown
en: What happens as we get older?
zh: 随着我们变老，发生了什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: is those switches kind of move around to the wrong places.
zh: 是那些开关移动到了错误的地方。

speaker: Unknown
en: And as those switches move around, that cell stops making the right protein and starts making the wrong protein, and it becomes dysfunctional.
zh: 当那些开关移动时，那个细胞停止制造正确的蛋白质并开始制造错误的蛋白质，并且变得功能失调。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if that happens in enough cells, then that tissue starts to misbehave.
zh: 如果这发生在足够多的细胞中，那么那个组织就开始表现异常。

speaker: Unknown
en: You get wrinkles.
zh: 你会长皱纹。

speaker: Unknown
en: Your heart can't beat quite right.
zh: 你的心脏跳动不太正常。

speaker: Unknown
en: Your retina doesn't pick up light as well and transmit the signal of the light, and things get blurry.
zh: 你的视网膜不能很好地接收光线并传输光线信号，东西变得模糊。

speaker: Unknown
en: Your hearing starts to lose.
zh: 你的听力开始下降。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can't think as quickly.
zh: 你思考没那么快了。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can't respond as quickly.
zh: 你反应没那么快了。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's what aging is.
zh: 这就是衰老。

speaker: Unknown
en: Aging is the core human disease.
zh: 衰老是核心的人类疾病。

speaker: Unknown
en: And as epigenetics, which is where the switches are on a cell, start to get moved around to the wrong place, and that tissue starts to misbehave, we get all these diseases.
zh: 随着表观遗传学——即细胞上开关所在的位置——开始被移动到错误的地方，且那个组织开始表现异常，我们就会得所有这些病。

speaker: Unknown
en: That could be one of the core drivers of cancer.
zh: 那可能是癌症的核心驱动因素之一。

speaker: Unknown
en: Why is aging so even across my body then?
zh: 既然如此，为什么衰老在我的身体里如此均匀呢？

speaker: Unknown
en: Because all these cells are suffering the same statistical effect of time as DNA breaks happen in every cell in your body.
zh: 因为所有这些细胞都在遭受时间的相同统计效应，因为 DNA 断裂发生在你身体的每个细胞里。

speaker: Unknown
en: And as those DNA breaks happen, those switches are moving around the same rate in all parts of your body.
zh: 当那些 DNA 断裂发生时，那些开关在你身体的所有部分以相同的速率移动。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's why parts of your body start to suffer kind of, it's like, oh my God, my hip hurts, my eye, my brain.
zh: 这就是为什么你身体的某些部位开始出现问题，就像，天哪，我的髋部疼，我的眼睛，我的大脑。

speaker: Unknown
en: Your young viewers may not appreciate this, but being 46, I'm starting to appreciate it.
zh: 你的年轻观众可能体会不到这一点，但作为 46 岁的人，我开始体会到它了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's becoming more of an issue.
zh: 这正变得越来越成为一个问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: a guy named Shinya Yamanaka discovered four proteins that you could put into a cell or apply to a cell.
zh: 一个叫山中伸弥的人发现了四种蛋白质，你可以把它们放入一个细胞或应用到一个细胞。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it would basically take all the switches in that cell and move them to the place that a stem cell has, which is basically an embryo in a human.
zh: 它基本上会拿那个细胞里的所有开关并把它们移动到干细胞所在的位置，这基本上就是人类的一个胚胎。

speaker: Unknown
en: And now that cell operates like an embryonic cell.
zh: 现在那个细胞就像胚胎细胞一样运作。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you can take that embryo cell and you can put other proteins on to move the switches around even more to turn that stem cell into an eye cell, into a skin cell, into a heart cell, into a lung cell, into a brain cell.
zh: 你可以拿那个胚胎细胞，你可以放上其他蛋白质来更多地移动开关，以把那个干细胞变成眼细胞、皮肤细胞、心脏细胞、肺细胞、脑细胞。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we suddenly developed this technology in the mid-2000s to take any cell and turn it into a stem cell, re-differentiated, it's called differentiation, from one cell type to another.
zh: 所以我们在 2000 年代中期突然开发了这项技术，可以把任何细胞变成干细胞，重分化，这被称为分化，从一种细胞类型到另一种。

speaker: Unknown
en: But then years later, another guy said, well, what if instead of putting a lot of that protein on the cell, we just put a little bit?
zh: 但多年后，另一个人说，好吧，如果不是在细胞上放大量那种蛋白质，我们只放一点点会怎样？

speaker: Unknown
en: So they took the Yamanaka factors, which are just four proteins, and they put a microdose of them on a couple cells.
zh: 所以他们拿了山中因子，也就是四种蛋白质，并在几个细胞上放了一个微剂量。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the switches started to move around, but they didn't move back to being a stem cell.
zh: 开关开始移动，但它们没有移回成为干细胞。

speaker: Unknown
en: What happened is they moved back to being a young version of that cell type.
zh: 发生的是它们移回了成为那种细胞类型的年轻版本。

speaker: Unknown
en: So the eye cell basically became a young eye cell.
zh: 所以眼细胞基本上变成了年轻的眼细胞。

speaker: Unknown
en: The skin cell became a young skin cell.
zh: 皮肤细胞变成了年轻的皮肤细胞。

speaker: Unknown
en: The heart cell became a young heart cell by putting a small dose of these proteins.
zh: 心脏细胞通过放置小剂量的这些蛋白质变成了年轻的心脏细胞。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it turns out that these proteins kind of move the switches around.
zh: 所以结果是这些蛋白质在某种程度上移动开关。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if you put just a small amount of them on, you can move the switches just back to the right position.
zh: 如果你只放少量它们，你可以把开关刚好移回正确的位置。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's now called epigenetic reprogramming.
zh: 这现在被称为表观遗传重编程。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's this new area of science that seems to indicate.
zh: 这就是这个似乎在表明的新科学领域。

speaker: Unknown
en: And they've now done it in mice where the mice can live to the equivalent of 100 plus years old.
zh: 他们现在在小鼠身上做了这个，小鼠能活到相当于 100 岁以上的年纪。

speaker: Unknown
en: They've put it on the tissue of monkeys and gotten rid of the wrinkles.
zh: 他们把它放在猴子的组织上并消除了皱纹。

speaker: Unknown
en: We now have just David Sinclair, just one of his companies did the dosing in the retina to reverse blindness in people with a retinopathy.
zh: 我们现在有了大卫·辛克莱，他的公司之一在视网膜上进行了给药，以逆转患有视网膜病变的人的失明。

speaker: Unknown
en: So this epigenetic reprogramming is an entirely new lane of medicine that says not just can we address all of the downstream effects of aging, but can we go to the core?
zh: 所以这个表观遗传重编程是一个完全新的医学路径，它说不仅我们可以解决衰老的所有下游影响，但我们可以直达核心吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Can we reset aging in all these cells in the body?
zh: 我们可以重置身体里所有这些细胞的衰老吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: And the answer so far is yes.
zh: 目前的答案是肯定的。

speaker: Unknown
en: The risk is if you reset it too much, it becomes an embryo and it turns into cancer.
zh: 风险是如果你重置得太多，它就变成胚胎并变成癌症。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that's what everyone's been working against in the last couple of years is how do you put the right dose of the right proteins in the right cells to get them to reverse their age and become young again?
zh: 这就是过去几年每个人都在努力攻克的问题，即你如何把正确蛋白质的正确剂量放在正确的细胞里，让它们逆转年龄并再次变年轻？

speaker: Unknown
en: And the path, it's really just an engineering exercise at this point, as opposed to a biological proof of concept.
zh: 而且这条路径，在这一点上它真的只是一项工程练习，而不是一个生物学概念验证。

speaker: Unknown
